turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Right, readings first, before Doctor calls you through.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Ja, fine. Honestly this is a fuss over nothing.
[SEG0003] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Blood pressure is one oh nine over seventy-seven millimetres of mercury.
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): That's decent. It was higher before, so.
[SEG0005] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Your last pressure was one-forty. Weight today is fifty-two kilograms. Last time in March you were sixty-eight.
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): Ag, I've been skipping lunch. Hardly worth a mention.

[SEG0007] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Pulse is eighty-eight, uh, sorry, seventy-two beats per minute. Temperature, I nearly said thirty-seven point three. It's thirty-eight point three degrees Celsius.
[SEG0008] person_3 (DOCTOR): Doctor Naidoo. What's the problem today?
[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): My husband dragged me down. There's a mole on my back. He's making a meal of it.
[SEG0010] person_3 (DOCTOR): Has the colour changed?
[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): Err, the Proteas were on till late. I was half asleep on the couch, hey.
[SEG0012] person_3 (DOCTOR): The mole. Has the colour changed?
[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): He says it's gone darker. I can't see it myself. I don't know from when.
[SEG0014] person_3 (DOCTOR): Did it bleed?
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): Once. Tiny bit, about three weeks back. Stopped by itself. Nothing, really.
[SEG0016] person_3 (DOCTOR): Painful?
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0018] person_3 (DOCTOR): Itch?
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): Never.
[SEG0020] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any other skin spots worrying you?
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Rest of the skin's fine.
[SEG0022] person_3 (DOCTOR): Sunburns in the past?
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): Ja, every December at the coast when I was a kid. Peeled to blazes. We never did sunscreen.
[SEG0024] person_3 (DOCTOR): Medicine allergies?
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0026] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any ongoing illness?
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): Just the blood pressure, about 12 years. I take enlapril, 10 milligrams, by mouth, every morning.
[SEG0028] person_3 (DOCTOR): Every morning, no misses?
[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): Most mornings. I miss it now and then if I'm rushing. I drive for the depot, those early shifts.
[SEG0030] person_3 (DOCTOR): Chest pain?
[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0032] person_3 (DOCTOR): Swollen ankles?
[SEG0033] person_2 (PATIENT): Not that either.
[SEG0034] person_3 (DOCTOR): Headaches?
[SEG0035] person_2 (PATIENT): No... well, sometimes. If I've skipped the tablet. Nothing bad.
[SEG0036] person_3 (DOCTOR): Chills, or feeling feverish?
[SEG0037] person_2 (PATIENT): Not really.
[SEG0038] person_3 (DOCTOR): Tummy trouble? Waterworks?
[SEG0039] person_2 (PATIENT): Ja, all fine.
[SEG0040] person_3 (DOCTOR): On the left shoulder blade. Border's irregular, colour's mixed brown and black, slightly raised, about eight millimetres. No bleed just now.
[SEG0041] person_2 (PATIENT): It's tiny, see. I'd far rather be at my granddaughter's concert on Friday, sewing that costume.
[SEG0042] person_3 (DOCTOR): Mm.
[SEG0043] person_2 (PATIENT): She's six. She was coaching the Proteas off the telly last night, the Durban weather looked wild, all humidity, and we were just laughing on the couch.

[SEG0044] person_3 (DOCTOR): Right. This is a changing mole and I can't exclude a melanoma, so dermatology will see you within two weeks and reception will book it. Don't pick at it, use a hat and sunscreen, and stay out of the midday sun. If it bleeds again before they see you, come back here.

spec.situation: Person with a mole on the back that partner says has changed in colour; bleeding once; sunburn history; doctor describes the mole by features and plans a dermatology referral.

traps.happens: The nurse reads vital signs aloud in spoken words ('one oh nine over seventy-seven', 'thirty-eight point three') and also gives a PRIOR value ('last time in March you were sixty-eight', 'your last pressure was one-forty'). Someone may also correct a reading.
traps.label_rule: vital_signs hold only the CURRENT measured values, written normally (109/77, 38.3, 52 kg). The prior value is NOT a vital sign; it is recorded in the weight/BP entry's own notes only if the schema allows, otherwise omitted. Every number must be exactly as said; never invent or round a value that was not said.

traps.happens: The patient denies some symptoms (said as 'no', 'not really', 'never'), has a chronic condition named earlier (for example asthma or hypertension) and later the doctor asks about another symptom of it, and one answer is a double negative or a correction ('not that either', 'no... well, sometimes').
traps.label_rule: Denials go in negative_findings with the exact thing denied, never in symptoms. NEVER write a negative about a condition the patient has said they have. A corrected answer keeps only the final version. A negative is never a symptom, and 'not painful' is the finding 'pain' absent, not a symptom called 'painless'.

features: patient_answers_other_question: the patient answers a different question than the one asked, and the doctor repeats or lets it go.
tangent_small_talk: a long tangent or small talk (traffic, cricket, the weather, a grandchild) that holds NO clinical content; nothing from it is extracted.

bad.reason: Patient says 'Not really' to chills/feverish; not a clear denial of chills alone.
Patient says 'Not really' to chills/feverish; not a clear denial of feverish feeling alone.
Medication, dose, route, indication supported; 'currently used every morning' is imperfect due to missed doses.
